**Hydrogen – A Quick Reference to Its Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Typical Value / Description |
|----------|----------|-----------------------------|
| **Basic Identity** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium) |
| | State at STP | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.9 °C (121 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.2 °C (14 K) |
| | Density (gas, 0 °C, 1 atm) | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume (ideal gas) | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | 0.754 eV |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Second ionization energy | 27.211 eV |
| | Heat capacity (gas, 25 °C) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat ratio (γ) | 1.41 (diatomic) |
| | Speed of sound (in H₂) | ~1270 m s⁻¹ (at 20 °C) |
| | Refractive index (air) | 1.000132 |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.792847 µB (proton) |
| | Nuclear spin | ½ (¹H), 0 (²H), ½ (³H) |
| **Chemical Behavior** | Oxidation state | +1 (most common) |
| | Common compounds | H₂O, H₂SO₄, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, etc. |
| | Acidic strength | Strong acid when bonded to electronegative atoms (e.g., HCl, H₂SO₄) |
| | Basicity | Weak base (hydroxide ion H⁻ is extremely reactive) |
| | Redox behavior | Reducing agent (e.g., H₂ + O₂ → H₂O) |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Bond length (H–H) | 0.74 Å |
| | Dipole moment (in H₂O) | 1.85 D (due to H atoms) |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Very high (e.g., in liquid ammonia, ethylene glycol) |
| **Physical & Thermodynamic** | Vapor pressure (at 25 °C) | 1.3 kPa |
| | Critical temperature | 33.0 K |
| | Critical pressure | 1.3 MPa |
| | Critical density | 0.31 g cm⁻³ |
| | Enthalpy of formation (gas) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Enthalpy of vaporization | 0.0899 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Enthalpy of fusion | 0.0005 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Heat of combustion (H₂ + ½O₂ → H₂O) | –285.83 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation (H₂O) | –237.13 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| **Spectroscopic** | Rotational spectrum | Microwave region (~2.1 THz for H₂) |
| | Vibrational frequency (H₂) | 4401 cm⁻¹ |
| | Electronic transitions | UV–visible absorption at ~121.6 nm (Lyman‑α line) |
| | Nuclear magnetic resonance (¹H NMR) | Chemical shift reference (TMS) |
| **Isotopic Variants** | ¹H (protium) | Stable, most abundant (≈99.98 %) |
| | ²H (deuterium) | Stable, 0.015 % natural abundance |
| | ³H (tritium) | Radioactive (half‑life 12.32 y), used in radiolabeling |
| | Deuterated compounds | e.g., D₂O (heavy water) |
| **Applications & Uses** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells) | Energy carrier, zero‑emission when used in PEMFCs |
| | Rocket propellant | Liquid hydrogen + liquid oxygen |
| | Metallurgy | Reducing agent for metal extraction |
| | Chemical synthesis | Hydrogenation, hydroformylation, etc. |
| | Analytical chemistry | NMR, mass spectrometry (H₂ gas as carrier) |
| | Medical imaging | ¹H MRI (proton imaging) |
| | Fundamental physics | Tests of quantum electrodynamics, proton structure |
| **Safety & Handling** | Flammability range (air) | 4 %–75 % (v/v) |
| | Explosion limit | 4 % (lower) – 75 % (upper) |
| | Toxicity | Non‑toxic; as a gas, it can displace oxygen leading to asphyxiation |
| | Storage | Cryogenic tanks (liquid H₂) or high‑pressure cylinders (gas) |
| | Environmental impact | Zero CO₂ emissions when combusted; requires careful handling to avoid leaks |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen is the simplest atom, with one proton and one electron.
- **Diatomic gas**: At room temperature, it exists as H₂ molecules.
- **Highly reactive**: Acts as a strong reducing agent and forms a wide variety of compounds.
- **Energy carrier**: Central to hydrogen fuel cell technology and rocket propulsion.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Protium, deuterium, and tritium each have unique nuclear properties and applications.
- **Safety**: Extremely flammable and can cause asphyxiation; requires proper storage and handling.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
